content_of_post_to_comment: Whenever I hear the claim that child readers are unable to identify with adult protagonists, I can't help but remember that The Hobbit, one of the most successful children's novels of all time, features a fifty-year-old bachelor as its hero.
comment: Maybe children don't need protagonists who resemble them in age so much as protagonists whose problems they can recognize. Bilbo's social awkwardness, fear, and desire for comfort are hardly exclusive to fifty-year-olds.
